clue.text: Holding fast had trouble lifting racket

indicators.note: to trouble something is to stir it up, so the letters of the word before it are disturbed into a new order
in a down clue lifting raises the word, so it is read upwards, from bottom to top

parts.note: a racket is a din or noise

explanation.surface: Someone clung on grimly while a racket went up around them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trouble' shuffles HAD into ADH; 'lifting' turns NOISE upwards in this down light, giving ESION.
explanation.definitionFit: Adhesion is the state of sticking firmly to something, which is what holding fast describes.

clue.text: New tea set in use for a liqueur?

indicators.note: new here means made afresh, so the letters of the following words are remade in another order

explanation.surface: A fresh set of tea things is pressed into service for serving after-dinner drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' rearranges the eight letters of TEA SET IN; 'use for a' just joins wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Anisette is a sweet aniseed-flavoured liqueur.

clue.text: Material of the hard shoulder () It can kill Brooklyn character, we hear

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held reads 'Material of the hard shoulder () It can kill Brooklyn character, we hear': the 4-down clue has been run into it and the real clue is cut short; no scan to restore it.
annotationWithheld.clue: Material of the hard shoulder () It can kill Brooklyn character, we hear

clue.text: It can kill Brooklyn character, we hear

indicators.note: we hear signals that what counts is how the word sounds when spoken, here in a Brooklyn accent

parts.note: a character is a person, and in a Brooklyn accent person comes out with an oy sound

explanation.surface: A deadly figure from Brooklyn, according to rumour.
explanation.walkthrough: The stereotyped Brooklyn (New York) accent turns the 'er' sound into 'oy', so 'person' is heard with that vowel.
explanation.definitionFit: A toxin is a substance that can kill, the classic murder weapon of detective fiction.

clue.text: Big eaters in schools

parts.note: reads like hungry pupils at a canteen, but the schools are groups of sea creatures and the big eaters are huge marine mammals

explanation.definitionFit: These vast marine mammals consume enormous quantities of krill and fish, and travel in groups called schools or pods.

clue.text: Dress for people up in Yorks or Hunts?

definitions.text: Dress for people up in Yorks or Hunts?

parts.words: Dress for people up in Yorks or Hunts?
parts.note: people up are those on horseback; Yorkshire was divided into Ridings and Hunts is short for Huntingdonshire, while hunts are also fox hunts

explanation.walkthrough: Yorkshire was historically split into three Ridings, and Hunts is the abbreviation for the old county of Huntingdonshire, so the counties hint at riding and hunting.
explanation.definitionFit: Jodhpurs, boots and a hacking jacket are the outfit worn by those on horseback.

clue.text: In the wild state, does he still remember?

definitions.text: In the wild state, does he still remember?

parts.words: In the wild state, does he still remember?
parts.note: plays on the saying that an elephant never forgets, applied to one that has gone wild and left the herd

explanation.definitionFit: A dangerous lone tusker that has turned savage and lives apart from its herd.

clue.text: Settling, perhaps donates in time

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the words could be arranged otherwise, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A gift paid over promptly may settle a matter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges the thirteen letters of DONATES IN TIME.
explanation.definitionFit: Sedimentation is the process of particles settling to the bottom of a liquid.

clue.text: Harmonises in "Grease" arrangement

indicators.note: an arrangement puts things in a new order, so the letters of the quoted word are reordered

explanation.surface: A singer blends voices in a new version of the musical Grease.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arrangement' looks musical, but it rearranges the six letters of GREASE.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that harmonise are in accord with each other, which is to concur.

clue.text: Voluntary work for the church?

parts.note: sounds like unpaid help for a parish, but a voluntary is an organ piece played in church, here the one at the end of the service

explanation.definitionFit: An organ piece played as the congregation leaves at the close of a service.

clue.text: English body of musicians get the bird

parts.note: MU stands for the Musicians' Union, the British trade union for musicians

explanation.surface: An English band is booed off stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get the bird' means be booed, which hides the definition 'the bird'.
explanation.definitionFit: A large flightless Australian bird.

clue.text: Some ogres I stand against, thus

clue.text: Condition of men solo, running to earth?

definitions.text: Condition of men solo, running to earth?

indicators.note: running water flows and moves, so the letters of the words before it are set in motion into a new order

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for earth, as on electrical plugs

explanation.surface: Men on their own, fleeing to ground, are in a sorry solitary state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'running' rearranges MEN SOLO, and E for earth is added at the end; the whole clue describes the solitary state.
explanation.definitionFit: Being alone and isolated, as men on their own going to ground would be, is to be solitary and sad.

clue.text: Work unit in power-generator

indicators.note: in tells us the answer sits inside the words that follow, spanning the hyphen

explanation.surface: A measure of work is found in a power station's generator.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across the hyphen: the end of 'power' and the start of 'generator'.
explanation.definitionFit: In physics this is a small unit of energy or work in the centimetre-gram-second system.

clue.text: Use soft soap for this woollen cloth

definitions.meaning: to soft-soap is to flatter or sweet-talk someone, evasive smooth chat
a soft loosely woven wool fabric, used for trousers and washcloths

explanation.surface: Using soft soap on a wool washcloth.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb the word means to talk evasively or flatter; as a noun it is a soft woven wool fabric.

clue.text: Lady taking orders runs up and down

indicators.note: in a down light the word reads the same whether you go up or down the column, so it is a palindrome

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A woman takes instructions while dashing up and down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking orders' means joining a religious order, not being told what to do.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman who has taken religious vows in a convent order.

clue.text: National shopkeepers' home?

parts.note: recalls the jibe, attributed to Napoleon, that the British were a nation of shopkeepers

explanation.walkthrough: Napoleon is said to have called the British 'a nation of shopkeepers'.
explanation.definitionFit: The country Napoleon mocked as a nation of shopkeepers is the home of those traders.

clue.text: All-points summit system of communication next year?

parts.note: all the compass points are N, E, W and S
a summit is a mountain's peak

explanation.surface: A high-level summit meeting sets up a new way of keeping everyone informed for the coming year.
explanation.walkthrough: The puzzle appeared in 1983, so 'next year' is 1984, Orwell's novel in which Newspeak is the state language.
explanation.definitionFit: The controlled language of the state in Orwell's novel Nineteen Eighty-Four.

clue.text: Art of calculation somehow it's chopping logic

indicators.note: chopping logic cuts into it, so the word logic is split open to take other letters inside
somehow signals the letters are put together in some other order

parts.note: the letters of it's, ignoring the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Somehow it amounts to quibbling, chopping logic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somehow' rearranges IT'S to IST, and 'chopping' puts that inside LOGIC, after LOG. To chop logic is to argue over fine points.
explanation.definitionFit: An old term for arithmetic or the science of reckoning, the practical part of calculation.

clue.text: Doing business, place notice in Herts town

indicators.note: in says one piece is placed inside another

parts.note: Tring is a market town in Hertfordshire (Herts)
an ad is a notice, short for advertisement

explanation.surface: A trader advertises in a Hertfordshire town to drum up custom.
explanation.walkthrough: Tring is a small market town in Hertfordshire, the county north of London abbreviated Herts.
explanation.definitionFit: Trading is buying and selling, the activity of commerce.

clue.text: For runner over five furlongs, see bookmaker at start of Sandown

indicators.note: start of picks out the opening letter of the word that follows

parts.note: read literally, a book-maker is someone who makes books, such as a printer

explanation.surface: Back a fast horse at Sandown, the racecourse, by finding a bookie at the start of the race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bookmaker' is not a bookie but someone who makes books. Sandown Park is an English racecourse, so the surface stays at the races.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse that races best over short distances such as five furlongs.

clue.text: Mass held on top of the world

definitions.text: Mass held on top of the world

parts.words: Mass held on top of the world
parts.note: sounds like a church service at the summit, but mass is a frozen mass sitting at the pole

explanation.definitionFit: A permanent sheet of frozen water covering a polar region.

clue.text: Unexpectedly let rip a peal of bells

indicators.note: unexpectedly suggests things happening out of order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The bells suddenly ring out loud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unexpectedly' rearranges LET RIP. In change ringing, triples are changes rung on seven bells.
explanation.definitionFit: In bell-ringing, a method rung on seven bells is called this.

clue.text: Home of the brave

parts.note: echoes the American anthem's line, but the brave is a Native American warrior and home is his tent

explanation.definitionFit: A dome-shaped dwelling of some Native American peoples, where a warrior called a brave lived.

clue.text: Silly fellow when soft-headed

parts.note: as can mean when, as in as I left

indicators.note: headed asks for the head, the first letter, of the word before it

explanation.surface: A foolish chap is soft in the head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'soft-headed' looks like one word meaning silly; split it, and 'headed' takes the first letter of 'soft'.
explanation.definitionFit: A fool or idiot, as in donkey-like stupidity.

clue.text: A bridge built at head of Conway is no flyover type

indicators.note: head of takes the first letter of the word that follows
built means constructed, so the letters are put together in a new structure

explanation.surface: A bridge put up near Conway, the Welsh town with a famous castle and bridges, is no flyover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'built' rearranges A BRIDGE into AGEBIRD, after C from the head of Conway. A flyover is a road bridge, but here it means a bird that flies.
explanation.definitionFit: A bird kept in captivity, which never flies over anything.

clue.text: Bit of a bloomer letting it slip out

indicators.note: out suggests being put out of order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A gaffe, letting a secret slip out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' suggests a blunder, but here it is a flowering plant. 'out' rearranges IT SLIP.
explanation.definitionFit: The female seed-bearing organ at the centre of a flower is part of a plant that blooms.

clue.text: Leaves the business of this estate overseas

definitions.text: Leaves the business of this estate overseas

parts.words: Leaves the business of this estate overseas
parts.note: reads as someone quitting the family estate abroad, but the leaves are the crop being grown as the business

explanation.definitionFit: An overseas estate, as in India or Sri Lanka, whose business is growing the leaves for brewing.
